sections.heading: Lore
sections.text:
"Hngh... Feels like the weight of the entire world has come down at me ... my knees, especially..."
 A member of Operations Team Z7 in Endfield, Estella handles intel gathering and communications. Physically weak, and shadowed by misfortune wherever she goes, she sometimes lets her sharp tongue and dark humor push outsiders away. Her dream is simple: to live a peaceful life. After all, she has seen too many people like herself, trapped in a world with no choices, no change, and no future.
 A life of danger and extremes has numbed her senses to the world and raised her threshold for stimulation. As a result, she sometimes seeks out harsher forms of challenge — like the pounding rush of heavy metal music. Those rare jolts give her a fleeting sense of change and something real.
 Through her work in Endfield, Estella hopes to make the world a little better and life a little easier for those around her.

sections.text:
Damage is split between Physical and Cryo, making scaling less efficient.

sections.heading: Kit Intro
sections.text:
Estella is a 4-star, Cryo, Polearm Support Damage dealer who has many strong abilities and effects, but all suffer from being split between two archetypes, Physical and Cryo-Solidification. This pulls her teams in two different directions, balancing out the power of her kit. Her element, Battle Skill, and Combo all Inflict or require Cryo in order to function, but the secondary effect of her combo and Ultimate both scale with and toward Physical.
 What makes Estella strong is that her Combo Skill applies Vulnerable for free, which is incredibly powerful. Her Ultimate is cheap, also applies Vulnerable and inflicts Physical Susceptibility, another great supportive bonus. All that sounds great, and it is in Physical teams. The catch is, to gain access to it, Estella must trigger her combo, which requires an enemy to become Solidified - a reaction not often found in Physical teams she’s designed to support. Characters like Alesh can help, and do allow the team to work, but aren’t enough to make up for the loss of playing pure element teams with a sole focus on one game plan.
 Right now, the Cryo-Physical hybrid archetype is lacking enough support to allow it to compete, leaving Estella as an alternative way to play other stronger teams for the time being.

sections.heading: Combo
sections.text:
Estella’s Combo Skill is her most powerful ability and also the reason she has to be played as a Physical-Cryo hybrid. The cause is its trigger requirement, which needs an enemy to be afflicted by Solidification. When used, causes Estella to deal Physical damage, some Stagger, and apply Lift, and if the enemy was Solidified, she’ll naturally Shatter them with said Lift and apply Physical Susceptibility for a short duration.
 This Combo Skill has many good effects, and without its tricky trigger requirement and the restriction around applying Physical Susceptibility would allow Estella a much more prominent position in the meta, but alas, that’s not the case. However, that doesn’t make her weak; it just makes her less flexible to build teams around.
 Potentials:
 Potential 1: Increases the duration of Physical Susceptibility significantly, making it more reliable and allowing it to boost the team's damage for longer even after your full combo has been executed.

sections.heading: Ultimate
sections.text:
Estella’s Ultimate isn’t as impactful as her Combo Skill, but continues to double down on her great supportive capabilities for the Physical element. Activating it only requires 70 energy (63 with potential 2), which is much cheaper than most characters' Ultimates.
 Upon use, it deals a large hit of Physical AoE damage, Stagger, and if the enemy is suffering from Physical Susceptibility, which they should be if you time it right, it inflicts Knock Down on all targets hit. Between this ability and Estella’s Combo Skill, she grants 2 Vulnerability and a reliable Physical damage buff, all without requiring any SP.
 Potentials:
 Potential 5: To make Estella’s low ultimate cost even more attractive, potential 5 also grants her an additional 5 energy every time an enemy becomes Solidified with a cooldown of 1s. Estella needs Solidification anyway, so this is essentially just free energy.

sections.heading: Battle Skill
sections.text: Compared to her Ultimate and Combo, Estella’s Battle Skill is far less impressive. All it does on use is deal damage in a line, hitting all enemies for some Cryo damage, Stagger, and applying Cryo Infliction to them. Not very exciting when considering the Physical side of her kit, but can be a useful tool for triggering or enabling Solidification. For this reason alone, it usually does see some use in most Estella teams, but if there’s ever a way to bypass needing to use it, most teams probably will.

sections.heading: Talents
sections.text:
Both of Estella’s talents are completely utility-focused. The first, Commiseration, grants a new Shatter synergy to her Battle Skill. Now, after Estella triggers a Shatter, her next Battle Skill will recover 15 SP on use, improving her and the team's SP efficiency. Not a game-changing talent, but still a nice bonus that is well worth unlocking.
 Note: The SP recovery effect is limited to one activation per Battle Skill; consuming multiple Shatters per Battle Skill will not return more SP.
 Estella’s other talent, Laziness Pays Off Now, is a very minor and niche defensive boost to her survivability when battling enemies that deal Cryo damage. It’s so minor, in fact, you’ll likely not notice its effect at all when playing, meaning whether you unlock it or not shouldn’t impact Estella’s main role in teams, making it entirely optional.

sections.heading: Gameplay
sections.text:
When playing Estella, here are a few things to look out for to make the most of her kit:
 Trigger Solidification by making use of Estella’s Battle Skill in combination with another Infliction or by relying on her teammates.

 Shatter Solidification with Combo Skill in order to apply Vulnerable to enemies. Align its use with the rest of your Physical-based rotation in order to take advantage of the Physical Susceptibility it applies.

 When available, use Ultimate after Estella’s combo in order to deal a large burst of Physical damage and apply even more Vulnerability stacks.

 Consume Vulnerability stacks with another teammate in order to apply Crush or Breach.

sections.heading: Best Weapons
sections.text:
Estella best Weapons are placed in order of what fits their playstyle the most . Check the comments to get additional context.

 1

 JET (P 0 )

 Estella's best in slot damage option by a very thin margin, despite it having multiple Arts DMG% boosts and most of Estella's damage being Physical. The reason it performs so well is due to its base damage and passive ATK%. With that said, it is not a huge upgrade over P5 OBJ Razohorn, meaning you don't have to chase it if you already have that.

 2

 OBJ Razohorn (P 5 )

 Estella's best 5-star option and also incredibly competitive with her best 6-star as well. It has two ideal passives and one that is good but only affects a part of her kit (Damage vs Cryo/Solidification). This, combined with the very strong Weapon Effect, puts this weapon at the top of Estella's wants list.

 3

 Valiant (P 0 )

 Another 6-star option for Estella, but one which performs worse than JET due to it having Agility as a part of its passives, a stat she can't use. Even factoring this in, the remaining passives plus this weapon's solid Weapon Effect are enough for it to claw back enough benefit for it to perform reasonably well, making it an option if you already have it levelled and don't have either of the above two options.

 4

 Mountain Bearer (P 0 )

 A 6-star stat stick which has incredibly wonky passives for Estella (wrong main stat), but which ends up being better than her F2P option despite that. It is mostly varied by the Physical DMG% and DMG% against Vulnerable enemies.

 5

 Aggeloslayer (P 5 )

 Last resort option if you're lacking any of the choices above. Has the correct passive stats, but all at much lower base values, setting it significantly behind all other choices.

 Teams and Synergies

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
Cryo

 Alesh Cryo

 Estella requires Solidification to function. Just by including Alesh, she can access it by combining her Battle Skill with his, which forcibly converts Cryo inflation into Ssolidificaiton

 Alesh provides great SP recovery

 Strong supportive set and weapon options which boost the team's damage

 Even more buffs for Endmin and the team after unlocking P3

 Can save Estella using her Battle Skill when his Ultimate is available, thanks to it applying Cryo Inflction, letting him use that, then his Battle Skill to apply Solidification instead of relying on her battle skill for Cryo

 Alesh deals physical damage with some of his abilities, which are buffed by Estella

 Physical

 Endministrator Physical

 Estella applies an outstanding amount of Vulnerability with her Combo skill and very cheap Utimate

 Estella applies Physical Susceptibility to boost the entire team's Physical damage

 Estella herself benefits nicely from Endmin’s teamwide buffs, boosting her own damage as well

 Estella unlocks a new way to play Physical teams Solidifaction-Physical hybrid

 Nature

 Ardelia Nature

 Able to permanently maintain both Arts and Physical susceptibility on targets for generic team-wide damage increases that work in any team

 Outstanding supportive weapon and set options for even more damage amplification, with options that work for both Physical and Arts

 Forcibly applies Corrosion, which, when optimized around, can lower enemy resistances to all damage temporarily if Susceptibility doesn't need to be refreshed

 Only requires 100 SP roughly every 30 seconds to function at maximum capacity

 Strong enough sustain to single handedly keep the team alive through most endgame encounters as long as smart dodging is used.

 Cryo

 Yvonne Cryo

 Estella is yet another Cryo Infliction applier who works with Yvonne, but who sets herself apart by trading a little of the SP efficiency of Last Rite and Snow Shine (has 85 SP cost Cryo instead of 70) for the ability to deal significantly more damage in the team.

 What gives Estella the edge in damage over other Cryo Infliction appliers is her Combo Skill, which, when used after Yvonne's Battle Skill, can trigger huge Shatters at very little opportunity cost (a little Crit DMG uptime in the time before Yvonne's Combo explodes).

 In addition to this, thanks again to her Combo Skill and also her Ultimate Estella also outputs above-average Stagger compared to alternatives, something which can be boosted further with an Arts Intensity build, a build that will also boost Shatter damage further.

sections.heading: Ultimate timings
sections.text:
Endministrator - Use Endmin's Ultimate directly after their Combo skill to ensure it consumes the Crystals to deal additional damage,
 Estella - Use Estella's Ultimate after her Combo skill but before you use Endmin's combo. This will apply an extra stack of Vulnerability and using it before Endmin's Combo will ensure you don't explode their crystals with it wasting them,
 Alesh - Use Alesh's ultimate either alongside Estella's Battle Skill or before your rotation starts. Just make sure you don't use it too soon during downtime as doing so will apply its Cryo Stack too early and disable Ardelia's combo from triggering,
 Ardelia - Save Ultimate for before one of your rotations, ideally during Stagger. Ardelia should be using Stanza Memoralis so using her Ultimate this way will buff the team.

sections.heading: Extra things to look out for
sections.text:
Against weaker enemies and those who struggle with sequencing all four characters at once, investing the time into establishing Ardelia's combo skill at the start of your rotation may not be worth it. Instead you can skip it and go straight to your physical rotation.

 Team #2

 Estella is a free-to-play, accessible unit that can supply steady Shatters to fuel Alesh's Combo Skill, all the while being able to flex multiple sets depending on the need: Eternal Xiranite for buffs owing to her Susceptibility, Swordmancer for stagger build, or even just Yinglung for damage. Between Alesh and Xaihi's buffs, this team is a non-premium alternative that can still perform surprisingly well.
 If enough Ultimate Gain Efficiency is on the table, can allow for condensed 4 Infliction, 3 Yvonne Battle Skill, 2 Yvonne Combo Skill rotations.

Her Ultimate is cheap, also applies Vulnerable and inflicts Physical Susceptibility, another great supportive bonus. All that sounds great, and it is in Physical teams. The catch is, to gain access to it, Estella must trigger her combo, which requires an enemy to become Solidified - a reaction not often found in Physical teams she’s designed to support. Characters like Alesh can help, and do allow the team to work, but aren’t enough to make up for the loss of playing pure element teams with a sole focus on one game plan.
 Right now, the Cryo-Physical hybrid archetype is lacking enough support to allow it to compete, leaving Estella as an alternative way to play other stronger teams for the time being.
 Combo
 Estella’s Combo Skill is her most powerful ability and also the reason she has to be played as a Physical-Cryo hybrid. The cause is its trigger requirement, which needs an enemy to be afflicted by Solidification. When used, causes Estella to deal Physical damage, some Stagger, and apply Lift, and if the enemy was Solidified, she’ll naturally Shatter them with said Lift and apply Physical Susceptibility for a short duration.
 This Combo Skill has many good effects, and without its tricky trigger requirement and the restriction around applying Physical Susceptibility would allow Estella a much more prominent position in the meta, but alas, that’s not the case. However, that doesn’t make her weak; it just makes her less flexible to build teams around.
 Potentials:
 Potential 1: Increases the duration of Physical Susceptibility significantly, making it more reliable and allowing it to boost the team's damage for longer even after your full combo has been executed.

 Ultimate
 Estella’s Ultimate isn’t as impactful as her Combo Skill, but continues to double down on her great supportive capabilities for the Physical element. Activating it only requires 70 energy (63 with potential 2), which is much cheaper than most characters' Ultimates.
 Upon use, it deals a large hit of Physical AoE damage, Stagger, and if the enemy is suffering from Physical Susceptibility, which they should be if you time it right, it inflicts Knock Down on all targets hit. Between this ability and Estella’s Combo Skill, she grants 2 Vulnerability and a reliable Physical damage buff, all without requiring any SP.
 Potentials:
 Potential 5: To make Estella’s low ultimate cost even more attractive, potential 5 also grants her an additional 5 energy every time an enemy becomes Solidified with a cooldown of 1s. Estella needs Solidification anyway, so this is essentially just free energy.

 Battle Skill
 Compared to her Ultimate and Combo, Estella’s Battle Skill is far less impressive. All it does on use is deal damage in a line, hitting all enemies for some Cryo damage, Stagger, and applying Cryo Infliction to them. Not very exciting when considering the Physical side of her kit, but can be a useful tool for triggering or enabling Solidification. For this reason alone, it usually does see some use in most Estella teams, but if there’s ever a way to bypass needing to use it, most teams probably will.
 Talents
 Both of Estella’s talents are completely utility-focused. The first, Commiseration, grants a new Shatter synergy to her Battle Skill. Now, after Estella triggers a Shatter, her next Battle Skill will recover 15 SP on use, improving her and the team's SP efficiency. Not a game-changing talent, but still a nice bonus that is well worth unlocking.
 Note: The SP recovery effect is limited to one activation per Battle Skill; consuming multiple Shatters per Battle Skill will not return more SP.
 Estella’s other talent, Laziness Pays Off Now, is a very minor and niche defensive boost to her survivability when battling enemies that deal Cryo damage. It’s so minor, in fact, you’ll likely not notice its effect at all when playing, meaning whether you unlock it or not shouldn’t impact Estella’s main role in teams, making it entirely optional.
 Gameplay
 When playing Estella, here are a few things to look out for to make the most of her kit:
 Trigger Solidification by making use of Estella’s Battle Skill in combination with another Infliction or by relying on her teammates.

 Shatter Solidification with Combo Skill in order to apply Vulnerable to enemies. Align its use with the rest of your Physical-based rotation in order to take advantage of the Physical Susceptibility it applies.

 When available, use Ultimate after Estella’s combo in order to deal a large burst of Physical damage and apply even more Vulnerability stacks.

 Consume Vulnerability stacks with another teammate in order to apply Crush or Breach.
